A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Graph2Eval and Graph2Eval-Bench. All 20 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original document and web-agent evaluations in Tables 2–3, task-generation timings, and an execution case study.

after.justification: v3 retains original agent evaluations and adds a KG-free ablation, UI-TARS results, graph-quality checking and human validation of the web-task evaluator.

M1.justification: KG construction, Algorithm 1's sampling rules, template and meta-path task generation, MMR selection and agent architectures remain substantively unchanged. Appendix A newly documents filtering and content constraints without establishing that the underlying procedure was changed.

E1.justification: Both retain the same 16 document sources, eight websites, 1,002 document tasks and 317 web tasks, with identical source and task-type distributions. The ablation uses the same source coverage; OSWorld and MMBench receive descriptive comparisons, not reported evaluations on additional datasets.

E2.justification: v3 introduces a directly evaluated KG-free task-generation baseline in Table 4, adding a central comparison absent from v1. Table 3 also adds UI-TARS-1.5-7B under both web-agent configurations. Tables 5–6 compare OSWorld, MMBench and TaskCraft descriptively rather than reporting numerical baseline runs.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 introduces 1,000 generated tasks per method, divided equally between document and web tasks, with GPT-4o generation and two human annotators assessing consistency and solvability. v3 also adds a 100-node-pair graph check and a 50-trajectory evaluator audit. The ablation's agent configuration is ambiguous: its prose names Gemini 2.5 Flash, whereas Table 4 lists Qwen models.

E4.justification: v3 adds a central ablation testing whether KG structure improves generated-task quality, plus graph-edge verification and human validation of web-task judgments. Conversely, v1's document task-type performance analyses in Figures 6–7 disappear. The execution case study and exploratory safety-generation discussion are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for performance. The new graph-precision and human–judge agreement percentages are point-estimate validation results, not uncertainty estimates for the reported scores.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports document/web consistency of 0.95/0.78 versus 0.74/0.62 without KG, and solvability of 0.93/0.72 versus 0.73/0.60. v3 also reports 88% graph-edge precision, 88% human–judge agreement, and UI-TARS overall success rates of 0.0491 and 0.0719. Existing Table 2 and retained Table 3 scores are unchanged, while document task-type results are removed.

T1.justification: The graph representation, sampling mathematics and existing metric formulas are retained. Carrying the relation set R consistently through Algorithm 1 and explaining the task-objective embedding clarify notation rather than introduce new theory. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: v3 makes improved semantic consistency and solvability central contributions, including claimed average improvements of 20% and 17% over baseline generation. v1 primarily emphasizes scalable generation and discrimination among agents. Its explicit claim to be the first framework automatically generating interactive web tasks is removed.

C2.justification: New Appendix D identifies dependence on accurate, complete KGs and restricted coverage beyond predefined relationships. Section 4.3 attributes KG-free multi-page failures to missing inter-page relations. The web-agent performance gap is newly interpreted as showing that the benchmark emphasizes multi-step reasoning rather than simple visual grounding.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds privacy/compliance filtering, prohibited task operations and BUSINESS_DATA placeholder details. The template difficulty list omits Expert, and single-agent error handling is relabeled partially supported. Conversely, v1's numerical coverage proportions disappear. Generation model, temperature, embeddings, evaluation prompts and project access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 substantially revises positioning around semantic consistency and executability, adds discussion of Learn-by-Interact, and contrasts Graph2Eval's graph-based generation with TaskCraft's task composition. New comparative tables cover TaskCraft, OSWorld and MMBench, additional benchmark literature is cited, and the first-automatic-web-task-generation novelty claim is withdrawn.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten around task quality. Existing experimental discussions are consolidated into Main Results, appendices are reordered, and duplicate task-template sections are merged. Terminology is standardized around document understanding and RAG/Web Agents.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. v1's overview diagram, coverage chart and document performance plots are removed; v3 adds Tables 4–6 and expands Figure 1 and Table 3 for UI-TARS. Retained figures are resized or relocated, and the source-distribution display and captions are corrected.

improvement.justification: v1 demonstrates benchmark use without directly testing the benefit of KG-based generation. v3 substantially addresses this deficiency through the KG-free ablation, graph-quality audit and human validation of web judging, while adding concrete limitations. These gains outweigh the lost task-type analyses and coverage proportions. Reporting remains imperfect: the ablation's Gemini/Qwen descriptions conflict, and Table 4 implies average human-score gains of 18.5 and 16 percentage points, not exactly the headline 20% and 17%.
